d4f672612d85: The oldest man we know for certain in the family. Smallholder, fisherman and beach bailiff in Økjær — a holding on land, nets in the sea and an office on the beach. Bought the house in Silkjær in 1854/55; in the deed to the Vedersø land of 1876 he appears as “Thomas Jensen Silkjær” — the earliest known record of the family name, which the newspapers’ death notice later repeated.

f16224204290: Smallholder and fisherman in Økjær like his father. In the oldest papers he is simply Niels Thomsen; in the later ones Niels Thomsen Silkjær; the name certificate of 1905 made the name legal, and the parish register of 1920 writes “smallholder Niels Silkjær”. With the farm name the family had, for the first time, a name that could be inherited.
c4b263fd8993: Entered in the levy roll in 1873 (levy district 28, Husby, letter Y, serial no. 5) as Niels Thomsen, son of the smallholder Thomas Jensen — 62¾ inches tall, about 164 cm. The board’s note in 1878: chest measurement 29½ inches, found exempt from military service and struck off the roll. The following year he stood at the lifeboat. [S113]
c0b1dc827966: 14 November 1878 — five days after his father’s death and three days before his funeral — to Ane Johanne Kristensen, b. 1843, twelve years older than he. 1079680a356a: The Dannebrogsmænd’s Badge of Honour, awarded on 10 November 1915 as serving boatman — in his thirty-seventh year at the station. He signed the oath of loyalty in Vedersø on 30 November 1915, and his own account of his life lies in the archive of the Chapter of the Royal Orders; after his death the cross was returned on 9 July 1928. The title Dannebrogsmand recurs in Dansk Fiskeristat 1935—36, and the badge is worn visibly in the portrait. [S8, S58, S111, S112]

8c4b0c8a3d2d: The parish book points to her parents as Jens Claus and Stine. The family file identifies them as Jens Claus Matzen, b. c. 1831 in Schleswig, and Ane Kirstine Hansdatter of Landtingmark; the full names have not been checked in the Ejsing parish register. The local history account records a schoolboy Jens Claus Mattzen in Husby — examined in arithmetic and discharged from school by the parish board on 15 April 1846, with the booklet’s remark that the foreign-looking spelling was probably owing to his birth and baptism in Angeln in South Schleswig. If the schoolboy is her father — name, parish and age fit — the family’s thread towards the duchies gains both a place and a figure; see caveat 09 [S171]
